edits.old: \item \textit{Note:} Coverage is the count within the closed 2.5th--97.5th percentile interval divided by the complete case count. Width and proper interval score are on the $\log(1+x)$ scale; lower interval score is better. edits.new: \item \textit{Note:} Covered is the number of USGS observations within the closed 2.5th--97.5th percentile interval divided by the case count. The numerical quantile conventions are specified in Appendix~\ref{app:numericalprediction}. The monotone inverse transformation preserves the stated coverage events. N, AL and exAL denote normal, asymmetric Laplace and extended asymmetric Laplace likelihoods. U and M denote one and multiple observation sources; T1 retains the transfer contribution at forecast leads and T0 omits it.

edits.new: \item \textit{Note:} Summaries concern the coefficient states $\boldsymbol\psi_T$ at the terminal historical date, for fitted probabilities $p_0=0.05$, $0.50$ and $0.95$. GDPC denotes the generalized dynamic principal component described in Section~\ref{sec:data}.

edits.old: \caption{Recorded stopping evidence for the existing benchmark and component-removal fits.}
edits.new: \caption{Stopping classifications for the model-comparison and component-removal fits.}

edits.old: \item \textit{Note:} Counts refer to individual quantile fits, or one fit per Gaussian run. Converged means the saved criteria or explicit summary report convergence; it does not certify model validity. Budget limit means recorded criteria were unmet at the iteration limit. Other covers guards or criteria-unmet stops; unrecorded means sufficient stopping evidence is absent. Pipeline completion and a legacy terminal success phrase do not establish convergence.
edits.new: \item \textit{Note:} Each fit corresponds to one target quantile, or one fit per normal model and origin. Converged indicates satisfaction of the recorded stopping criteria; this classification does not establish model adequacy. Iteration limit indicates that these criteria were not jointly satisfied before the limit. Other includes numerical safeguards or other stops with unmet criteria. Unrecorded indicates insufficient stopping information, rather than demonstrated failure. The component suffixes are defined in Table~\ref{tab:he3_ablation_crps}. N, AL and exAL denote normal, asymmetric Laplace and extended asymmetric Laplace likelihoods. U and M denote one and multiple observation sources; T1 retains the transfer contribution at forecast leads and T0 omits it.

edits.old: \item \textit{Note:} All scores use $\log(1+x)$. The adjusted pairwise score assumes independent, identically distributed draws from a predictive distribution. For physical members this is only a sensitivity assumption. Model sample counts are 2,000 for AL/exAL, 64 for N-U-T1 and 48 for N-M-T0/T1; raw GloFAS and NWS contain 51 and seven members. edits.new: \item \textit{Note:} Empirical CRPS scores the equally weighted empirical predictive distribution; adjusted denotes the pairwise correction under independent, identically distributed predictive draws. Scores use $\log(1+x)$ discharge, with $x$ in m$^3$/s. For physical ensemble members, independence is a sensitivity assumption. Sample counts are 2,000 for AL/exAL, 64 for N-U-T1 and 48 for N-M-T0/T1; GloFAS and NWS contain 51 and seven members. The adjustment is inapplicable to deterministic climatology and EMOS grids and to the persistence point mass; adjusted skill is not reported. N, AL and exAL denote normal, asymmetric Laplace and extended asymmetric Laplace likelihoods. U and M denote one and multiple observation sources; T1 retains the transfer contribution at forecast leads and T0 omits it.
